title: When the Hollow Turns
premise: Rosalind Sterling, exiled from the storm-caller citadels for a betrayal she barely remembers committing, has spent ten years guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains. When a mute child arrives at her cabin speaking Vessic — a language that died with the Hollow War three centuries ago — Rosalind discovers the girl carries a living memory-seed: the complete recollection of the atrocity that started the war, hidden inside her by dying priests. The seed is waking, and both the resurrected Hollow Court and Rosalind's former order want it. Pursued through the mountains she knows better than anyone, Rosalind must choose between destroying the seed to save the child and letting it bloom to expose the truth that could reignite the war — or finally end it. In the end, Rosalind sacrifices her own scattered memories to anchor the seed safely, learning that the betrayal she was exiled for was a lie planted in her mind; she returns the child to the rebuilt Vessic sanctuaries and walks into a future she must now remember honestly.
about_author: Cyrus Oyelaran is a former cartographer who spent six years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction, a background that infuses his landscapes with unsettling precision. He writes fantasy about memory, exile, and the geography of guilt from a home he refuses to locate on any map.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Knocked Twice
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A storm-caller living quietly above the smuggler roads, Rosalind finds a frostbitten child on her doorstep during a whiteout. The girl speaks no known tongue, yet Rosalind half-understands her. Emotional beat: wary solitude cracked open by an inexplicable pull of responsibility.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Consulting a forbidden lexicon, Rosalind identifies the language as Vessic, dead since the Hollow War. That night the girl sleep-speaks a place-name Rosalind has only seen in sealed archives. Beat: dread replacing curiosity as the impossible becomes documented fact.

chapters.title: Smoke on the North Pass
chapters.summary: POV of Dain Ferro, a smuggler captain and Rosalind's oldest client. He reports soldiers burning waystations along the north passes, asking questions about 'a small passenger.' Beat: the outside world closing in, loyalty to Rosalind tested against fear.

chapters.title: What the Order Buried
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She breaks into an abandoned storm-caller vault seeking answers and finds records of the memory-seed ritual — and her own name listed among the priests who performed it, though she remembers none of it. Beat: vertigo of self-doubt; her exile suddenly feels engineered.

chapters.title: Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: POV of Sereth, a revenant agent of the resurrected Hollow Court, tracking the seed across the mountains. Through his eyes we see the enemy's patience and its hunger. Beat: chilling escalation — the Court knows exactly where the child is heading.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Dain offers to move Rosalind and the girl south through his safest route, but demands she use her storm-calling openly to shield his caravan — exposure she swore never to risk. Beat: the first hard trade between safety and secrecy.

chapters.title: Thunder Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ambushed by Court wraiths at the Saddle Rocks, Rosalind calls a storm for the first time in a decade; it comes too easily, too eagerly, frightening her more than the enemy. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear of what she still is.

chapters.title: The Seed Wakes
chapters.summary: POV of the child, Wren, rendered in fragmentary sensory prose. Inside her, the memory-seed blooms: she experiences the Hollow War atrocity as if it were happening now, screaming in Vessic. Beat: horror and tenderness — a child carrying a nation's worst night.

chapters.title: An Old Debt in Ironhollow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Sheltering in a mining town, Rosalind seeks out Maren Kestrel, a disgraced archivist who once studied the seed ritual. Maren confirms the truth can be read without being unleashed — but only at the Hollow Gate, deep in Court territory. Beat: hope with a terrible price tag.

chapters.title: The Order Finds Her
chapters.summary: POV of High Cantor Ilvane, Rosalind's former mentor, arriving under a flag of truce. Ilvane claims the Order wants to protect Wren and gently implies Rosalind's lost memories hold the key. Beat: seductive manipulation; the reader senses the trap before Rosalind does.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Lies
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Comparing Ilvane's account with the vault records, Rosalind realizes her 'betrayal' was implanted — she was exiled to hide her connection to the seed's creation. Dain urges her to trust no one. Beat: rage and grief; the ground of her identity gives way.

chapters.title: Wren Runs
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wren and Dain. Terrified by a nightmare-bloom of the seed, Wren flees into a blizzard toward the Hollow Gate alone, compelled by the memories inside her. Dain finds her half-frozen. Beat: panic and the depth of Dain's reluctant love for the child.

chapters.title: The Court's Invitation
chapters.summary: Sereth's POV. The Hollow Court captures the caravan but, surprisingly, lets them go — delivering an invitation: bring the seed to the Gate willingly, or they will take it and the child. Beat: dread reframed as choice; the enemy wants consent for reasons unknown.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Maren admits she helped design the seed's hiding ritual centuries ago — she is far older than she appears — and that it can be destroyed, but the destruction will kill whoever anchors it. Beat: the true cost named aloud; loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Night at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close POVs (Dain, Wren, Maren) over one night of rest before the Gate. Quiet conversations, a shared meal, Wren teaching Dain a Vessic lullaby. Beat: the calm before catastrophe; everything they stand to lose made warm and specific.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate Road
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ilvane returns with Order forces, revealing the truce was cover: the Order intends to seize the seed and erase it — and everyone who knows of it. Dain takes a mortal wound covering their escape. Beat: betrayal crystallized; grief and fury fused.

chapters.title: Into the Hollow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Carrying Dain's body and leading Wren and Maren through the Court's dead lands, Rosalind confronts hollowed echoes of her own erased memories walking the landscape. Beat: descent — literal and psychological — toward the truth beneath her exile.

chapters.title: The Memory-Seed Blooms
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the Hollow Gate, the seed fully opens: Wren relives the war's founding atrocity in full, and the reader finally sees it — an act committed jointly by the Order and the old kings, then blamed on the Vessic. Beat: devastating revelation; the war's true history laid bare.

chapters.title: Storm Against Silence
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ilvane and Sereth converge on the Gate. Rosalind unleashes everything she is, calling a storm vast enough to hold both armies at bay while Maren prepares the rite. Beat: climax of power and principle — violence in service of witness, not vengeance.

chapters.title: The Price of Remembering
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. To keep the bloomed truth from killing Wren, Rosalind anchors it herself, feeding the rite her own memories — including the false ones, which burn away, and true ones she chooses to give. Beat: sacrificial climax; she saves the child by unmaking parts of herself.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The revelation spreads; the Hollow Court, given the acknowledgment it sought for centuries, stands down; the Order fractures as Ilvane's role surfaces. Maren guides Wren to the surviving Vessic sanctuaries. Beat: bittersweet victory — truth costs, but it ends rather than ignites the war.

chapters.title: When the Hollow Turns
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue. With gaps where her past used to be, Rosalind visits Wren in the sanctuary and begins writing down what she now knows, choosing to rebuild her identity from verified truth. Wren speaks her first word of common tongue: Rosalind's name. Beat: quiet resolution — survival's price paid, memory chosen anew.
